stem: When grossing an appendectomy specimen for clinical history of appendicitis, sectioning does not reveal any masses but does reveal 2 lymph nodes. Which of the following would be the most appropriate sections to submit?

options.text: All lymph nodes are submitted in their entirety
options.explanation: All lymph nodes are submitted in their entirety. Appendix specimens often have either too many lymph nodes or none at all. If a lymph node or 2 is identified, it has to be submitted for microscopic examination in order to evaluate the possibility of metastatic tumors, either from the appendix or elsewhere in the body.

options.text: Lymph nodes > 1 cm are submitted in their entirety
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

options.text: No lymph node submission is necessary, as no mass has been identified grossly
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

options.text: Representative sections of all lymph nodes
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

options.text: Representative section of appendix, along with the area of perforation and surgical margin
options.explanation: Representative section of appendix, along with the area of perforation and surgical margin. Submitting the appendiceal margin in appendectomy specimen for acute appendicitis is recommended, since on occasion one may encounter a neoplasm upon microscopic evaluation that was not apparent during grossing.

options.text: Representative section of appendix and surgical margin
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

stem: Which of the following is true about GISTs of the appendix?

options.explanation: Likely more common in women. GISTs of the appendix are rare. The largest series of them included twice as many female patients as male patients.
like at other sites, appendiceal GIST is almost always positive for DOG1.

options.text: Often large with abundant mitotic activity
options.explanation: appendiceal GISTs are almost always small with minimal mitotic activity.
appendiceal GISTs typically have KIT mutations.

stem: This mesenchymal tumor was found incidentally within an appendix removed for appendicitis. What immunohistochemical stains would most likely be positive in this tumor?

options.explanation: This lesion is a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), as evidenced by the bland spindled cells, perinuclear vacuoles and skeinoid fibers. The appendix is a rare location but as with GISTs elsewhere in the gastrointestinal tract, they are positive for CD117 and DOG1 by immunohistochemistry.
Leiomyoma, not GIST, would be positive for desmin and SMA.
Schwannoma, not GIST, would be positive for S100.
Neuroendocrine tumor, not GIST, would be positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin.

stem: Which clinical scenario is most likely associated with the histologic diagnosis of the appendectomy specimen shown above?

options.text: Acute appendicitis managed with immediate surgery
options.explanation: this is not an acute inflammatory process; acute appendicitis with immediate surgery would not show the chronic inflammatory process of xanthogranulomatous appendicitis (foamy, lipid laden histiocytes, mixed inflammatory cell infiltrates, fibrosis and dystrophic calcifications).
there is no evidence of tumor.

options.text: Complicated appendicitis treated with antibiotics followed by interval appendectomy
options.explanation: Complicated appendicitis treated with antibiotics followed by interval appendectomy. The histologic image shows xanthogranulomatous inflammation of the appendix, which is usually associated with interval appendicectomy.
pediatric viral gastroenteritis primarily affects the small intestines, not the appendix as shown in the image.

stem: Which histologic feature distinguishes malakoplakia from xanthogranulomatous appendicitis (shown above)?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

options.text: Intracytoplasmic granules in histiocytes with positive PAS stain
options.explanation: Intracytoplasmic granules in histiocytes with positive PAS stain. While both malakoplakia and xanthogranulomatous inflammation are associated with chronic inflammatory conditions, they are histopathologically distinguished by the presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies in malakoplakia with positive PAS and von Kossa stains.

stem: A 20 year old man with known cystic fibrosis presents with abdominal pain localized to the right lower quadrant. Imaging reveals an enlarged, mucus filled appendix. What is the most likely histologic finding in the appendix of this patient?

options.explanation: Appendiceal dilation with inspissated mucus. Cystic fibrosis often leads to mucus obstruction in the appendix, resulting in appendiceal dilation and mucus impaction with or without acute inflammation.
epithelial dysplasia with fibrotic changes is not a hallmark of cystic fibrosis in the appendix.
hyperplasia of lymphoid tissue is unrelated to cystic fibrosis related appendiceal changes and is more typical in lymphoid hyperplasia.
although mucinous neoplasms can present with appendiceal dilation, they do not typically arise as a result of cystic fibrosis.

stem: A 44 year old man with cystic fibrosis presents with abdominal pain and distension. Surgery reveals a distended appendix filled with inspissated mucin. A representative histologic image is shown above. What complication is most commonly associated with these findings in cystic fibrosis?

options.explanation: appendiceal adenocarcinoma is a neoplastic process that invades the appendiceal wall and often presents as a mass forming tumor.

Appendiceal perforation. Inspissated mucus in cystic fibrosis can obstruct the appendiceal lumen, leading to increased intraluminal pressure and secondary inflammation, which commonly results in appendicitis. On very rare occasions, this can cause perforation.
carcinoid tumors are unrelated to mucus retention and appendicitis seen in cystic fibrosis patients.
mucinous neoplasms are not a typical finding in cystic fibrosis related appendix pathology.

stem: An 11 year old boy undergoes appendectomy for dilated appearing appendix on imaging. What is the most likely diagnosis for the histologic appearance shown above?

options.explanation: neutrophilic inflammation is absent.
granulomas are absent.
Lymphoid hyperplasia. The image depicts marked hypertrophy of lymphoid follicles within the lamina propria, which is characteristic of lymphoid hyperplasia.
the lymphoid infiltrate does not efface normal structures and is polymorphic without significant cytologic atypia.

stem: Appendiceal lymphoid hyperplasia is characterized microscopically by which of the following features?

options.explanation: epithelioid granulomas are not a feature of lymphoid hyperplasia.

options.text: Prominent lymphoid aggregates containing follicles expanding the lamina propria
options.explanation: Prominent lymphoid aggregates containing follicles expanding the lamina propria. Lymphoid hyperplasia is characterized by prominent lymphoid aggregates containing follicles (typically including clusters > 10) in the lamina propria layer.

in lymphoid hyperplasia, prominent lymphoid aggregates are predominantly restricted to the lamina propria, whereas transmural lymphoid aggregates may be seen with interval (delayed) appendectomy or Crohn's disease.
transmural neutrophilic inflammation is a feature of acute appendicitis, not lymphoid hyperplasia.

stem: Which of the following factors affect the staging of appendiceal neuroendocrine tumors?

options.text: Ki67 index and extent of local spread

This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

options.text: Size and extent of local spread
options.explanation: Size and extent of local spread. These are used to determine pT category staging; pT1 - pT3 include size and pT3 - pT4 include local spread.
This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

stem: An appendiceal neuroendocrine tumor develops clinical metastatic disease to the liver but no other sites. What is the cM category staging for this tumor?

options.explanation: it suggests there is no distant metastatic disease.
cM1a. Metastatic disease only to the liver is considered M1a for appendiceal neuroendocrine tumors.
M1b requires metastasis to nonhepatic distant sites.
M1c requires distant metastasis to both hepatic and extrahepatic sites.

options.text: When a tumor extends to the surgical resection margin
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Review the correct-answer explanation and the linked PathologyOutlines topic for why this distractor does not fit.

options.explanation: When a tumor has cellular intraperitoneal metastases. Such cases are stage IV and they may be subclassified as IVA or IVB depending on the tumor grade.

options.text: When a tumor involves the muscularis propria
options.explanation: tumor grade does not impact pT category staging of appendiceal adenocarcinomas.

options.text: When a tumor is a goblet cell adenocarcinoma

stem: What is the difference in AJCC staging parameters for low grade apendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN) and high grade apendiceal mucinous neoplasm (HAMN)?

options.text: LAMN cannot be pM1a but HAMN can
options.explanation: both LAMN and HAMN can be pM1a.

options.text: LAMN cannot be pN1 but HAMN can
options.explanation: both LAMN and HAMN can theoretically be pN1 (though this is extraordinarily unlikely).

options.text: LAMN cannot be pT1 / 2 but HAMN can
options.explanation: LAMN cannot be pT1 / 2 but HAMN can. LAMN is reported as pTis(LAMN) if bound by muscularis propria, whereas HAMN would be pT1 or pT2 in the same situation, depending on whether submucosa or muscularis propria is involved.

options.text: LAMN cannot be pT4a but HAMN can
options.explanation: both LAMN and HAMN can be pT4a.

stem: A 31 year old man presenting with right lower quadrant pain, fever and radiologic evidence of acute appendicitis undergoes appendectomy, which reveals the findings above. What is the most likely clinical risk factor?

options.explanation: recent antibiotic use is not a risk factor for CMV infection, though may predispose other infections, such as C. difficile.
HIV infection. Immunocompromised states like HIV infection or history of solid organ transplantation are risk factors for CMV infection.

the patient's clinical presentation is not typical of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), though patients with IBD may be at increased risk for CMV infection, particularly after steroid therapy. Answer E is incorrect because travel outside the U.S. may predispose to certain infections (e.g., parasitic) but it is not a risk factor for CMV infection.
trauma is not a risk factor for CMV infection.

stem: Which histologic feature is characteristic of CMV appendicitis?

options.explanation: Intranuclear and intracytoplasmic inclusions. The presence of basophilic intranuclear inclusions (owl eye inclusions) and intracytoplasmic inclusions are characteristic of CMV infected cells.

options.text: Luminal amoebae with foamy cytoplasm and ingested erythrocytes
options.explanation: these features are typical of Entamoeba histolytica infection.
these features are typical of measles (rubeola virus) infection.

options.text: Rod shaped bacteria in the appendiceal lumen
options.explanation: rod shaped bacteria in the appendiceal lumen are nonspecific and may not be pathogenic. Answer E is incorrect because these features are typical of adenovirus infection.

stem: A 44 year old woman underwent screening colonoscopy. The endoscopist noted a polypoid mass arising in the cecum and performed endoscopic polypectomy. The findings are pictured above. Which of the following is a key microscopic feature of this entity?

options.explanation: the presence of ganglion cells is a key to the identification of muscularis propria.
the presence, rather than absence, of submucosal adipose tissue is a microscopic feature of inverted appendix.

options.text: Ganglion cells embedded in thick smooth muscle bundles
options.explanation: Ganglion cells embedded in thick smooth muscle bundles. The presence of thick smooth muscle bundles of muscularis propria containing ganglion cells and nerve fibers is a key microscopic feature.
the lesion is typically elongated, polypoid or dome shaped rather than sessile.

stem: A 56 year old woman with a history of cecal mass on imaging underwent partial cecectomy with appendectomy. The gross findings are pictured above. What is true of this diagnosis?

options.explanation: It is associated with endometriosis. The lesion shown is an inverted appendix, which can occur without any underlying abnormality or may be associated with anatomical variations or pathologic conditions, such as endometriosis or appendiceal neoplasm.

options.text: More common in men than women
options.explanation: inverted appendix is more common in women than men.

options.text: Resection of the lesion is necessary for the diagnosis
options.explanation: though it may be diagnostically challenging in some cases, it is possible to diagnose on radiographic imaging or colonoscopy.

options.text: Resection was inappropriate management for this patient
options.explanation: appendectomy with resection of cecal cuff is generally recommended for inverted appendix to avoid recurrence.

stem: A 20 year old man presented to the emergency department with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness, vomiting, fever and anorexia. Appendectomy with clinical diagnosis of acute appendicitis was done and histologic examination is shown in the image above. What is the diagnosis?

no diverticula are identified.
Granulomatous appendicitis. This section shows the formation of multiple granulomas.
mucocele is a clinical diagnosis referring to a dilated appendix.

stem: A 17 year old boy presented with mild right lower quadrant abdominal pain, malaise and mild fever for 2 weeks. He was diagnosed with ruptured acute appendicitis and was treated with antibiotics. He presented 2 months after for an appendectomy. Histologic evaluation of the appendix revealed chronic inflammation and multiple granulomas. What is the most likely underlying cause of granulomatous appendicitis in this patient?

options.explanation: Crohn's disease rarely involves the appendix.
Interval appendectomy. Interval appendectomy is an important cause of granulomatous inflammation in the appendix. Clinical history is the main clue in this scenario.
sarcoidosis often shows well formed nonnecrotizing granulomas. Presence of a clinical history is helpful.
tuberculosis often presents with systemic symptoms and necrotizing granulomatous inflammation.

options.explanation: Signet ring cell type is associated with a worse prognosis. The clinical and histological findings suggest appendiceal signet ring cell adenocarcinoma, which is associated with a worse prognosis compared to other types of appendiceal adenocarcinoma.

They can cause intussusception. Intestinal type adenomas of the appendix can cause appendicitis, bowel obstruction or perforation. stem: A 32 year old woman with history of hematuria coinciding with her menstruation underwent an appendectomy for an incidentally discovered dilated appendix. On gross exam, the appendix appeared dilated. Sectioning revealed a dilated mucin filled lumen with no evidence of neoplasms. What histological findings are supportive of an endometriosis involving an appendix?

options.text: Complex villous proliferation of appendiceal epithelium
options.explanation: complex villous proliferation of appendiceal epithelium refers to a high grade mucinous neoplasm.

options.text: Flat proliferation of mucinous epithelial cells
options.explanation: flat proliferation of mucinous epithelial cells suggests a mucinous neoplasm, likely a low grade appendiceal neoplasm (LAMN).

options.text: Monotonous infiltration of small round cells with speckled nuclei
options.explanation: monotonous infiltration of small round cells with speckled nuclei suggests a neuroendocrine tumor.

options.text: Unremarkable appendiceal epithelium with focal fibrosis and nests of endometrial stroma
options.explanation: Unremarkable appendiceal epithelium with focal fibrosis and nests of endometrial stroma. This patient is presenting with signs of endometriosis. Endometriosis and focal scarring may obstruct the appendix, causing dilation of the lumen and mucus build up.

There is no evidence of infection, inflammatory bowel disease or other significant medical history. H&E image showed a benign appendix with transmural chronic inflammation. options.explanation: Interval appendicitis is characterized by histologic features of a chronic inflammatory process, such as the presence of scattered granulomas, xanthogranulomatous inflammation, and macrophages laden with hemosiderin, among others. Interval appendectomy is performed in selective patients with risk factors but not in most patients (see Treatment section). It has a wide spectrum of histological findings including acute inflammation. Crohn’s-like features can often be seen in interval appendectomy specimen. Comment Here Reference: Interval appendicitis

stem: A 45 year old woman presents with a 2 week history of abdominal pain and increased abdominal girth. Clinical and radiologic findings are concerning for pseudomyxoma peritonei. A biopsy from an omental nodule is shown. The primary neoplasm is most likely from which anatomic site?

options.explanation: Appendix. Pseudomyxoma peritonei is a clinical syndrome characterized by extravasation of mucin into the abdomen due to a ruptured mucinous neoplasm. Primary tumors from all of the sites listed have been associated with pseudomyxoma peritonei. However, the large majority arise from the appendix. Furthermore, the low grade cytology displayed in the image strongly argues for a low grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm primary. Comment Here Reference: Pseudomyxoma peritonei

stem: Based on the WHO (5th edition) grading system of peritoneal metastases of appendiceal mucinous neoplasms, which of the following is a feature of grade 2?

options.explanation: Destructive invasion. The WHO (5th edition) recommends a 3 tier system for grading peritoneal disease of primary appendiceal mucinous neoplasia (grade 1 - 3). The grade of peritoneal disease has prognostic significance and guides therapeutic interventions. Hypocellular deposits with low grade cytology is classified as grade 1. Hypercellular deposits with high grade cytology or destructive invasion is classified as grade 2. Finally, grade 3 requires infiltrative signet ring cells. Importantly, degenerative cells floating in pools of mucin that morphologically resemble signet ring cells are not associated with a poor prognosis and do not warrant categorization as grade 3. Comment Here Reference: Pseudomyxoma peritonei

stem: Which of the following criteria below should be used to stage the appendiceal tumor in this patient?

options.explanation: Extent of invasion. Goblet cell adenocarcinoma behaves (and thus is graded and staged) like adenocarcinoma. Grading should be based on the proportion of low and high grade components. This case would be considered low grade since there is > 75% tubular growth and < 25% high grade component on the representative slide. Purely assessing percentage of glandular formation is used to grade traditional colorectal adenocarcinoma. Mitotic activity and Ki67 proliferative index are used to stage neuroendocrine tumors and should not be used to grade goblet cell adenocarcinomas. Size is used to stage neuroendocrine tumors.
